summary: Intermittent artifact fetch failures and control-plane 401s when traffic egresses via VPCE behind branch TAP/mirroring
environment: prod us-east-1 / branch-office DMVPN to on-prem transit
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using our Private deployment with a VPCE in front of on-prem serving nodes report intermittent artifact fetch failures (range GET 403/401 and occasional TLS resets) originating from branch office users connected over a DMVPN tunnel. Impact:
- Affects model shard downloads for large-range GETs (typically >1MB) from certain branch offices.
- Causes control-plane auth retries and token refresh 401s for some requests leading to degraded inference for affected customers.
Environment:
- Private deployment, VPCE in us-east-1, branch offices via DMVPN to customer transit.
- Serving nodes behind internal NLB, long-lived gRPC connections for streaming.
Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) From a branch office client, start a large batch inference workload that triggers sharded artifact downloads.
2) Several downloads complete; some requests fail with HTTP range 416/403 or gRPC stream reset.
3) Re-running sometimes succeeds; outage windows are intermittent and correlate with scheduled branch TAP/mirroring windows.
Observed logs and captures:
- Control plane logs show token refresh 401s coinciding with artifact download failures.
- tcpdump from a serving node shows duplicate TCP segments with identical sequence numbers arriving in short bursts; ClientHello appears duplicated in pcap (two ClientHello records separated by a tiny delta).
- NLB metrics showed connection churn and short-lived rehandshakes during the windows.
- VPCE logs show ALPN negotiation succeeded initially but downstream TLS session failed during renegotiation attempts.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Morales (Reporter): Customer submitted ticket. Provided initial pcap and timeline from branch office IT. Noticed correlation with nightly TAP job on customer's branch firewall appliance.

2026-03-10 13:30 - Liam Chen (Assigned): Acknowledged receipt; requested full tcpdump (pcap) and VPCE flow logs. Asked customer to confirm whether branch tap/mirroring is active during failure windows.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Customer (BrightEdge NetOps): Confirmed branch port-mirroring to an IDS is enabled for nightly compliance scans; they disabled mirror for a 30-minute test window and reported transient improvement.

2026-03-11 09:45 - SRE (J. Alvarez): Packet analysis shows duplicated segments and immediate retransmits with unusual MSS/TS behavior. Hypothesis: in-line mirroring device is injecting or replaying packets causing TCP reassembly corruption on our NLB/serving nodes.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Liam Chen: Routed to Networking vendor contact; attempted mitigation by advising customer to disable mirroring for branch or route artifact fetches via an alternate NAT path that does not traverse the mirrored segment.

2026-03-13 08:10 - Customer: Implemented alternate egress route around mirror for artifact hosts; observed no failures in a 6-hour smoke window. Asking for a recommended permanent fix and detection for future incidents.
investigation_notes: Collected pcaps from customer and from serving node at time of failure. Matched packet timestamps: duplicate TCP sequence numbers present with differing MAC-level source addresses (mirror copies).

Examined NLB connection logs: SYN/ACK handshake completes; duplicates arrive post-handshake, triggering our TCP stack to see out-of-order segments and occasionally drop TLS records. This causes TLS client hello duplication and server-side handshake reject (we observed 'early_data_mismatch' on some nodes).

Checked VPCE and S3 presigned URL validation: presigned signatures remained valid; 403/401 were downstream artifacts from replays and token refresh failures caused by aborted TLS sessions, not credential issues.

Reproduced by enabling port mirroring in a lab environment against a test VPCE and our NLB: enabling mirror produced the same duplicate-sequence symptom and intermittent shard range failures for large downloads.
Temporary mitigation validated: routing artifact downloads via a NAT egress path that avoids the mirrored segment prevented duplicates and eliminated failures in test and production smoke window.

Customer's IDS appliance vendor indicates a firmware bug in their mirroring engine that can 'reinject' mirrored packets under high load. Vendor provided firmware 4.3.2-beta that claims to fix duplicate injection; customer planning controlled upgrade.
Recommendation to Engineering: add lightweight detection on serving nodes for burst duplicate sequence deltas and log an explicit metric when observed to aid automated alerting and faster triage.
root_cause: On-prem branch TAP/port-mirroring appliance was reinjecting mirrored packets into the branch DMVPN path under load, producing duplicate TCP segments. Duplicates caused TLS record reassembly issues at the NLB/serving nodes, leading to aborted handshakes, token refresh 401s, and intermittent artifact range failures.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: customer rerouted artifact fetch traffic through an alternate NAT path that does not traverse the mirrored/span segment; failures stopped during the monitoring window. Customer scheduled vendor firmware upgrade for the mirroring appliance (recommended stable release after vendor QA).
Permanent actions and follow-ups:
- Customer to upgrade mirroring appliance; confirm with us after upgrade and provide post-upgrade pcaps.
- Engineering to create an internal detection metric for duplicate TCP sequence bursts (ticket INT-3307 created).
- Ops runbook updated with steps to identify packet reinjection (pcap signatures, NLB metrics to check) and suggested temporary routing workarounds.
- Follow-up: validate whether VPCE/NLB can be hardened to drop duplicates earlier (investigation ticket opened with infra team: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/742).
next_steps: 2026-03-14: Customer will upgrade mirroring appliance to vendor-stable firmware and run a 24-hour validation window; will provide pcaps post-upgrade.
2026-03-15: Engineering to scope and prioritize detection metric work (INT-3307) to add to serving-runtime agent; target P2 for next sprint if low-risk.
notes: This ticket is expected to resolve after customer confirms post-upgrade validation and after we land duplicate-detection telemetry. Keep P1 until customer signs off production stability.
